title: Quantization profile orchestration and artifact lifecycle for Console calibration jobs
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Problem statement: Teams running quantization workflows (FP8/INT8) need a single place in Redwood Console to launch calibration jobs, store and discover resulting quantization profiles and artifacts, manage retention costs, and apply fine-grained permissions so that sensitive artifacts are not exposed. Current gaps: artifacts are scattered (S3 buckets + ad-hoc PR notes), no standard metadata for reproducibility, and no UI for bulk retention/cleanup. This ticket sculpts the end-to-end product surface for calibration job orchestration: run lifecycle, artifact schema, retention defaults, RBAC controls, promotion workflows to model-serving variants, and accuracy/regression validation gates.
acceptance_criteria: Console UI: users can create a calibration job from model page with inputs for dataset, quantization targets (FP8/INT8), seed, and compute profile
Runs: every calibration run is persisted as a first-class object with immutable metadata (model_version, code_hash, dataset_version) and a stable run_id
Artifacts: quantization profiles, calibration traces, and accuracy reports are stored and searchable in Console with tag filtering
Retention: admins can set org-level and project-level retention policies (7/30/90/365 days) and apply overrides per-run
Permissions: RBAC rules allow roles to create runs, view artifacts, or promote profiles; audit log entries are generated for promotion and deletion events
API: public REST endpoints exist for listing runs, downloading artifact bundles, and triggering re-calibration via API/CLI
Validation: a post-run accuracy report is generated and shown with a pass/fail gate against configured thresholds
Reproducibility: each artifact bundle includes a manifest with toolchain versions and kernel selection hints
notes: 2025-02-14: Kickoff with runtime and infra leads. Discussed dedup key for artifacts (model_version + dataset_hash + quant_config).
2025-02-20: Design review: added explicit 'promotion' step to avoid accidental serving of unvalidated profiles. Link to design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/CAL/Quant+Artifact+Lifecycle
2025-02-26: Eng prefers 90-day default retention to balance cost and debuggability. Need opt-out for PII-sensitive customers.
2025-03-01: Security asked for KMS-wrapped artifact storage option and field-level audit events for delete/promote operations.
2025-03-04: UX iteration: add bulk 'archive' action and soft-delete with 14-day undelete window before hard purge.
api_endpoints: GET /api/v1/calibrations/:run_id/artifacts -> list artifact files and signed URLs
POST /api/v1/calibrations/:run_id/promote -> mark profile as candidate for serving
rbac_roles: calibration_creator: can create runs and view artifacts they created
calibration_viewer: can view run metadata and read artifacts (project scope)
calibration_admin: can modify retention, hard-delete, and promote profiles
auditor: read-only view + access to audit logs for promotions/deletions
retention_policy_summary: Default org retention 90 days for artifact bundles. Project owners can set 7/30/90/365 or infinite. Runs can be tagged 'keep-forever' which requires calibration_admin approval. Soft-delete holds artifacts for 14 days before permanent deletion. Cost-savings mode will auto-archive bundles to cheaper storage (glacier) after 30 days.
ui_workflow_summary: Flow: Model page -> 'Run calibration' modal -> select dataset/version, quant target (FP8/INT8), compute profile -> optional tags and retention override -> create. Calibration list view supports filters (status, quant target, pass/fail), bulk archive/restore, run-detail page with artifacts, accuracy graphs, and promotion button guarded by a validation checklist.
run_metadata_schema: Each run records: run_id, created_by, created_at, model_name, model_version, code_hash, dataset_name, dataset_hash, quant_target, seed, compute_profile, kernel_hints, toolchain_version, accuracy_metrics, status (queued/running/succeeded/failed/archived), artifact_urls
logging_audit_requirements: Every create/promote/delete/hard-delete action emits an audit event with user, timestamp, action, target_run_id, ip_address. Promotion events must record baseline_accuracy and promoted_profile_id. Audit logs retained per org security policy (default 365 days).
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (week 1): API + DB schema + storage layout + basic UI to create/list runs (beta). Phase 2 (week 2): artifact search, retention UI, RBAC enforcement, audit events. Phase 3 (week 3): promotion workflow, validation gates, CLI support, and org-level retention settings. Beta rollout to select customers on dedicated plan before org-wide GA.
open_questions: Should we expose kernel selection hints to end-users or keep it internal to runtime? Pros: reproducibility; Cons: increased surface area for confusion.
How to index large accuracy traces for fast UI playback without exploding DB size? Consider precomputed summaries and offloading raw traces to object storage.
What API rate limits are required for bulk downloads of artifact bundles to prevent egress storms?
Do we allow cross-project artifact reference for multi-tenant projects that share datasets?
